title: A deprecated declaration names its replacement as a checked Novis expression, every use warns with that rewrite as its fix, and a `// TODO:` comment is a list the tools print
scope:
the compiler-recognized `#[Core\Deprecated]` attribute, its attach sites, its `replace` template and
the checks the template meets where it is declared; `W1003` at every use and the rewrite it carries as
a `safe` suggestion; the `// TODO:` comment form; `nvs check --deny`, `--fix` and `--todos`; and the
`[errors] deprecated` setting with `Core\DeprecatedError`. The spelling of each new diagnostic, and
the exact text of `W1003`'s message, are left to the stages that write them.
dependsOnText:
[0046](0046.md) (attributes, which left `#[Deprecated]` to its own record), [0068](0068.md)
(a forced break is announced by a warning naming its replacement), [0099](0099.md) (a quick fix is a
diagnostic's suggestion), [0137](0137.md) (no `@deprecated` tag), [0064](0064.md) (the block roster).
validatedBy:
`tests/conformance/reject/a-deprecation-template-that-does-not-fit-does-not-compile.nvst`, and the
goal `deprecated-and-todo`'s acceptance checks: every fixture the rewrite tests fix is checked again
with no `W1003` and no error, and a program that uses nothing deprecated compiles to the same code.
